title: Wax thermostat
object: Automotive wax-pellet coolant thermostat (opens at 88 °C) in section, in its housing between engine and radiator
idea: A setpoint controller with no electronics: negative feedback through melting wax
summary: Paraffin in a brass cup gains 12 % in volume as it melts, squeezes a rubber sleeve and pushes the pin against the bridge, so the cup moves down: the valve opens to the radiator and the bypass disc shuts. The engine's heat balance closes the loop, and the coolant settles a little above 88 °C, higher under load. Wax freezes 2 K below where it melts, so the lift–temperature diagram traces a hysteresis loop.
usedFor: Automotive technician training: cooling systems, thermostat faults, bypass and jiggle valve
Control engineering teaching: proportional control, droop, hysteresis and feedback without electronics
Product documentation for wax-element actuators and thermostatic valves
views: Detail D jiggle valve and seat 5:1
